title: Cross-tenant Isolation & Hardware Noise Mitigation — Arch Review
content:
Meeting date: 2025-07-18
Facilitator: Elena Garcia
Attendees: Elena, Marcus, Priya, Owen, Sara, (recording in #eng-serving-runtime)
Duration: 60m
Location: Zoom (link in calendar)

Purpose / Context:
- Recap: multiple production incidents this quarter showed P99 latency spikes correlated with seemingly unrelated tenant work on shared GPUs (esp. heterogeneous workloads: long-context chat vs short embeddings). Team suspects "hardware noise" (thermal throttling, power governor shifts, SM frequency oscillation) is coupling tenant performance. We need an architecture-level approach to limit cross-tenant interference while keeping utilization and cost-efficiency.

Quick telemetry snapshot (what we observed):
- Healthy baseline: 8–12ms per-token on p99 for short seqs on A100-class nodes.
- Incident samples: p99 jumped to 40–120ms for minutes, aligned with a co-located tenant starting repeated long-context generation jobs. No obvious network or scheduler failure.
- GPU metrics: transient SM clock drops (~10%), occasional power-limit throttles, and GPU utilization oscillation. Host metrics showed CPU steal and RNIC queue length spikes.
- Correlated indicators: KV cache eviction rates rose for the affected tenant, leading to extra kernel work.

Problem statement (concise):
- How do we architect tenant isolation to make noisy co-tenants unable to cause >x% regression to a tenant’s latency p99, while avoiding large utilization loss?

Options discussed (pros/cons):
1) Strict physical isolation (one-tenant-per-GPU / per-node)
   - Pros: simplest correctness; eliminates hardware noise unless at node-level.
   - Cons: high cost, low utilization for bursty workloads. Operational friction for Dedicated customers.

2) MIG / instance-level partitioning where supported
   - Pros: strong hardware-level isolation for A100 and later; good utilization when tenant workloads small.
   - Cons: MIG availability limited across fleet and cloud partners; some models incompatible with partitioning; extra complexity in placement.

3) Soft isolation via runtime policies (cgroups + CPU/GPU affinity + per-tenant GPU power caps)
   - Pros: incremental deployable; can be tuned per-customer SLA; maintains multiplexing.
   - Cons: does not prevent hardware-level thermal coupling fully; requires careful telemetry and control-plane knobs.

4) Noise-aware scheduler + tenant throttling
   - Pros: dynamic, can detect noisy tenants and steer/cooldown them; preserves overall utilization.
   - Cons: reactive; detection is noisy and can cause oscillation if not damped.

5) Pre-warm / KV affinity + workload shaping
   - Pros: reduce extra kernel work during interference windows by keeping hot KV locally; cheaper mitigation for short seq burst impact.
   - Cons: only addresses cache-eviction amplification, not raw thermal throttling.

Decision and priorities (consensus):
- Short-term (Q3): adopt a combined soft-isolation + noise-detection approach (options 3 + 4) so we can ship mitigations quickly without fleet rework. Key pieces:
  - Per-tenant host CPU pinning for driver and runtime subprocesses to reduce CPU steal.
  - Introduce per-tenant soft power and SM governor hints where cloud APIs allow; default conservative caps for free-tier/unknown tenants.
  - Implement a noise-detector that raises a "noisy-tenant" flag when we see correlated clock drops + sustained tail latency delta (>2x baseline) and KV eviction bursts.
  - Scheduler will prefer relocating noisy tenants off mixed high-priority shared racks or to spare capacity zones using existing capacity-cutover playbooks.

- Medium-term (Q4): expand MIG-capable tiers for Dedicated and Dedicated+ customers and offer a "noisy isolation" add-on. This requires fleet inventory and deployment automation.

- Long-term (next 2 releases): explore hardware telemetry SLAs with cloud partners and per-node temperature/clock agreements; research per-tenant thermal partitioning with vendors.

Implementation notes and design details (actionable):
- Telemetry changes (owner: Marcus Li; ticket INFRA-1284):
  - ingest SM clock, power limit events, GPU temperature, KV eviction counters at 1s granularity to our TSDB for 90d.
  - new composite signal: "hardware-noise-index" computed as weighted z-score of clock-drop events + eviction-rate + RNIC queue rate.

- Runtime changes (owner: Priya Menon; PR linked):
  - introduce a soft-isolation policy API in the runtime config: cpu_pinning: [host-cpus], gpu_power_limit_hint: int, migration_priority: low|normal|high.
  - when noisy-tenant flag is set, runtime will gracefully reduce preemption windows and enable aggressive KV pinning to local slab where possible.

- Scheduler and placement (owner: Owen Clarke):
  - extend spot/evacuation logic to prefer relocation of noisy tenants first; add damping windows to avoid thrash.
  - add placement constraints to prefer MIG nodes when tenant requests "isolation add-on".

- Observability / SLOs (owner: Sara Ahmed):
  - dashboard: per-tenant hardware-noise-index and p95/p99 latency deltas.
  - alert: noisy-tenant > threshold for 3m triggers automated migration plan + oncall page.

Open questions / risks (short list):
- How will soft power hints interact with cloud provider autoscaling and internal power capping? Need cloud partner consult.
- MIG not supported for all instance types — what’s the upgrade path for older Dedicated customers?
- Risk of unfair noisy-tenant classification (false positives) causing customer-impacting migrations. We need a rollback window and customer-notification mechanism.
- Cost modeling: estimate utilization loss if we enforce 1 GPU per 2-tenants vs current multiplexing levels. (Action: finance link request)

Action items (owners + due dates):
- Marcus: prototype hardware-noise-index + dashboard (P0) — due 2025-07-31 (INFRA-1284)
- Priya: runtime soft-isolation API prototype + unit tests — due 2025-08-08 (PR: /runtime/pull/312)
- Owen: scheduler damping + migration plan (dry-run) — due 2025-08-15 (INFRA-1290)
- Sara: SLO/alert thresholds proposal and oncall playbook update — due 2025-07-28
- Elena: vendor/cloud partner outreach for MIG and power-control APIs — due 2025-07-25

Notes / Misc:
- We agreed to keep customer communication cautious; don't announce product changes until we have validated noisy-tenant detection with 2 weeks of historical data.
- Cross-team sync: Platform-engineering and Private-deployments leads invited to next follow-up (calendar invite sent).

Appendix (short logs):
- Example trace id: rwd-prod-20250710-7f3 (attached in internal ticket) — shows clock drop followed by 60s of p99 spike and then slow recovery as KV cache warmed.
- Reference: earlier playbooks on capacity-cutover and eviction-detection were helpful; we will reuse parts.

Status: notes captured here; next meeting scheduled 2025-07-25 to review initial telemetry prototype.

End of notes.
